articles.title: Reverse-engineered games: All the news on video game decomps, recomps, VR and web and 3D ports
articles.excerpt: It’s a wild time for retro gaming. Thanks to decompilations and recompilations of classic titles, those games are becoming unshackled from their proprietary code and original hardware to be ported to…
articles.body: It’s a wild time for retro gaming. Thanks to decompilations and recompilations of classic titles, those games are becoming unshackled from their proprietary code and original hardware to be ported to new devices or updated in ways to completely change the original game. Ever imagined skateboarding in Call of Duty ? Or playing the original Halo right in your web browser , complete with multiplayer? These are unofficial versions of games, so they may sit in a legal gray area. It seems unlikely that Nintendo, for example, is particularly happy about people finding ways to play The Legend of Zelda on non-Nintendo hardware.

articles.title: OutingFold: a pocket field guide that shows what Gemma left out
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass. OutingFold turns park notes into a small field guide you can fold and take outside. Paste the source text, let…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 1: Touch Grass . What I Built OutingFold turns park notes into a small field guide you can fold and take outside. Paste the source text, let local Gemma suggest useful excerpts, review the selection, then save an offline page or print it. The card has places for practical details, things to look and listen for, cautions, and a detail you notice yourself. It is for a short visit where a few source excerpts would be useful and another open browser tab would not. The difficult part was deciding what a model should be allowed to put on that page. A fluent summary can drop the second half of a warning. An exact quotation can do the same thing if it leaves out the next sentence.

articles.title: Cheap App Logging for Small SaaS: Compare Hosted and Self-Hosted Failure Signals
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for a small SaaS notification service, the best inexpensive logging choice is the one that preserves enough evidence to reconstruct a failed delivery without turning every retry into a f…
articles.body: Short answer: for a small SaaS notification service, the best inexpensive logging choice is the one that preserves enough evidence to reconstruct a failed delivery without turning every retry into a fresh incident. Start with a compact event schema, separate attempt facts from final outcomes, retain an audit trail keyed by an idempotency key, and compare Datadog, Better Stack, Logtail, Axiom, and self-hosted Loki with the same replayable dataset. Price matters only after the candidates produce equivalent answers. Signal quality comes first. A payment receipt that fails once, succeeds on retry, and is later logged as both "failed" and "sent" can mislead support, reconciliation, and compliance review.

articles.title: (Rant) Provenance and npm packages
articles.excerpt: Here's the thing about me. I'm an overbearing asshole. As such, I don't really like npm. No good reason to speak of. I've dabble with yarn and pnpm, and internal npm registries, and lockfiles and sha…
articles.body: Here's the thing about me. I'm an overbearing asshole. As such, I don't really like npm. No good reason to speak of. I've dabble with yarn and pnpm, and internal npm registries, and lockfiles and sha hashes and IPFS and all that. I've gone a long time from actually using npm proper. Like, the public npm registry. And I had seen the yarn npm registry (mirror?). I'm like... "that's cool, but how can they stay in sync? like, a publish to yarn isn't going to make it into npm, because npm doesn't read from yarn." So in no future world will some exclusive "yarn only" ecosystem evolve, where collaborations of npm packages exclusively state that, you know, you can't install stuff unless you use the yarn registry. So yarn is never going to become an alternate or a competitor to npm.

articles.excerpt: Changing a customer's name should not require remembering which DAO to call after every assignment. Loading twenty orders should not accidentally fetch each customer's entire history. Those are the ki…
articles.body: Changing a customer's name should not require remembering which DAO to call after every assignment. Loading twenty orders should not accidentally fetch each customer's entire history. Those are the kinds of problems that appear once an application grows beyond a few independent tables. What is Codename One? Codename One is an open-source framework for building native iOS, Android, desktop, and web apps from a single Java or Kotlin codebase. Learn more at codenameone.com . Last week's ORM example introduced shared entities and generated DAOs. This release adds a managed session: an object that keeps track of the entities involved in one unit of work, detects their changes, and coordinates persistence. Relationships now belong in the model too.
